metadata.title: US presses Apple to avoid Chinese memory chips amid shortage - WSJ reports

content.text:
Investing.com -- The Trump administration has urged Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) not to purchase memory chips from Chinese manufacturers as the iPhone maker seeks supplies amid an AI-driven shortage, the Wall Street Journal reported exclusively on Friday.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said he had directly told Apple that the administration opposed major US companies sourcing memory from China.
Apple has been testing chips made by ChangXin Memory Technologies and Yangtze Memory Technologies for possible use in devices sold in China, according to people familiar with the matter.
Demand from companies building AI data centers has created a shortage of memory chips and driven prices higher. The increased costs have pushed Apple and other consumer-electronics manufacturers to raise product prices.
Apple Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan declined to confirm that the company was testing Chinese chips. He said the scale of the shortage meant Apple had to examine all available options, including helping existing suppliers expand US production.
US regulations require American companies to obtain licenses before sharing product information with CXMT or YMTC. Such information would be needed to manufacture customised chips for Apple.
Apple can still purchase standard, off-the-shelf components from the Chinese companies and negotiate prices with them.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) has asked the administration to prevent Apple from using Chinese memory, arguing that such purchases would hurt domestic manufacturing and conflict with Washington's semiconductor reshoring goals.
Senators representing states where memory-chip producers plan to expand also wrote to Apple CEO Tim Cook in July, urging the company not to work with the Chinese suppliers.
The dispute creates a new source of tension between Apple and the administration, which has been pressing the company to move more of its supply chain to the US.
Washington has secured an agreement for Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) to manufacture some Apple chips and a commitment for iPhone and Apple Watch cover glass to be produced domestically.
Apple has also expanded Mac Mini assembly in Texas, but most of its supply chain remains in Asia, with the company increasing iPhone production capacity in India
